Compare 2 large blue-black birds, both in the Crows and Ravens (Corvus) genus and Crows, Jays, and Magpies (Corvidae) family:

American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos)
Common Raven (Corvus corax)

xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx

COMPARE American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) and Common Raven (Corvus corax):
Both are highly intelligent. Crow is smaller 45cm (17 inches) long; Raven is up to 61cm (24 inches) long. Raven rides the thermals and soars, whereas crow does more flapping. Raven tail resembles a wedge, compared to the rounded fan-like shape of the crow. Crow tail feathers are the same length, so when the bird spreads its tail, it opens like a fan. Raven has longer middle feathers in the tail, so tail appears wedge-shaped (pointed) when open. Crow walks… Raven has a 2-footed hop. Raven has a long, heavy bill. Upper half of bill slopes more downward than a crow bill. Ravens tend to be solitary or in pairs. Crows prefer flocks of 2+ individuals.
American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) has narrower pointed bill. Head is large in proportion to bill. Hackles are minor and only ruffled with vocalization.

Ravens have a wide range of vocalizations and they communicate often with flock members. Ravens have a deeper, lower pitch, croacking voice. Sometimes they say what sounds like "hawk, hawk."
Crows have higher pitch voice, more of a "cah, cah" sound.

Crows, Jays, and Magpies (Corvidae) family: 22 genera; 136 species worldwide:
Corvidae are medium to large passerine birds with strong, straight bills often slightly curved at the tip. They have robust bodies, rounded wings, and relatively short tails compared to other songbirds. Plumage is usually black, blue, or gray, sometimes with iridescence, and sexual dimorphism is minimal. They possess strong legs and feet adapted for walking and manipulating objects. Vocalizations are varied and complex, with many species capable of mimicry. Behaviorally they are highly intelligent, showing problem-solving skills, tool use, and complex social structures. Nests are typically bulky and built in trees, and most species are omnivorous, feeding on insects, seeds, carrion, and small vertebrates.

Corvidae "includes some of the most familiar birds in the world. Ravens and crows figure in the mythologies of many peoples worldwide, and they are well known for their sociality and intelligence. The family boasts the most advanced avian tool-user, the New Caledonian Crow Corvus moneduloides. Somewhat like parrots, corvids have calls that commonly are raucous and harsh, but many are capable mimics of a wide variety of other species’ syllables, sometimes strung together in a “whisper song” audible only at close range. Dismissed often as common familiar black birds, corvids include some stunningly beautiful birds; some of the magpies and treepies are among the most elegant and graceful of all the world’s birds."
